## Summary

I moved the hardcoded English copy on `/login` and `/register` into the app's translation catalog and added a parallel Japanese catalog, so both pages now render in Japanese when a browser's `Accept-Language` header prefers `ja`.

**Changes:**
- `lang/en/auth.json` (new) — English `auth.login.*` and `auth.register.*` keys, wording unchanged from today.
- `lang/ja/auth.json` (new) — Japanese counterparts, exact strings from the spec.
- `lang/ja/messages.json` (new) — Japanese `welcome` key (`「:nameへようこそ！」`), keeping the `:name` placeholder.
- `resources/js/pages/auth/Login.tsx` / `Register.tsx` — replaced literal strings with `useTranslation()`'s `t('auth.login.*')` / `t('auth.register.*')` calls (from `@guren/inertia-client`), including the `<Head title>` tab title.
- `src/app.ts` — added `'ja'` to `i18n.supported`, which turns on the framework's built-in `Accept-Language` detection (query param and cookie still take priority, matching existing behavior).
- `.guren/translations.gen.ts` — regenerated via `bun run codegen` (20 keys, `en`/`ja`).
- `tests/AuthI18n.test.ts` (new) — exercises the actual locale-resolution scenarios from the task (ja variants, no header, en-preferred, English-outranks-Japanese, unsupported `fr`), plus exact-string checks for both catalogs.

Verified `bunx guren check --i18n` reports full key parity between `lang/en` and `lang/ja`, `bun run typecheck` is clean, and `bun test` passes (13 tests, including the 11 new ones). Everything else (Layout/header, controllers' validation/redirect logic) is untouched, so English visitors and the sign-in/register flow behave exactly as before.
